[Problem on LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/biggest-single-number/)

## Problem

`MyNumbers` is a single column of integers, possibly with repeats. A single number is one that appears exactly once. Report the largest single number, or `null` if there is none.

## Formalisation

The table is a multiset $T$, which is exactly a set together with a multiplicity function

$$
\mu(n) = \big|\{\, t \in T \mid t = n \,\}\big|.
$$

`GROUP BY num` with `COUNT(*)` computes $\mu$: one row per distinct value $n$, carrying $\mu(n)$. The single numbers are the preimage

$$
S = \mu^{-1}(\{1\}) = \{\, n \mid \mu(n) = 1 \,\},
$$

and the answer is $\max S$, with the convention $\max \emptyset = \mathrm{NULL}$. SQL follows this convention: an aggregate over an empty set returns one row containing NULL.

## Solution

```sql
WITH dist AS (
  SELECT num, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM MyNumbers
  GROUP BY num
)
SELECT MAX(num) AS num
FROM dist
WHERE cnt = 1;
```

The same query with a subquery and `HAVING`, which filters the groups directly:

```sql
SELECT MAX(num) AS num
FROM (SELECT num
      FROM MyNumbers
      GROUP BY num
      HAVING COUNT(*) = 1) AS singles;
```

## Pitfalls

- **A CTE body is a full query.** My first attempt wrote `WITH dist AS (num, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM ...)` without the `SELECT`.
- **`ON d.num = d.num` compares a table with itself.** It is true for every row, so the join pairs every row with every row, a Cartesian product. The condition should link the two tables (`i.num = d.num`), and here no join is needed at all, since `dist` already has one row per number.
- **`MAX` handles the empty case; `LIMIT` does not.** `ORDER BY num DESC LIMIT 1` returns no rows when there are no single numbers, but the problem wants one row containing `null`. `MAX` over an empty set gives exactly that.
- **`WHERE` filters rows, `HAVING` filters groups.** In the CTE version, `cnt` is an ordinary column of `dist`, so `WHERE cnt = 1` works. Inside the grouped query itself, the condition on `COUNT(*)` has to go in `HAVING`.
